item.text: {"text":"Recent work supports aligning textual and collaborative representations, but offers limited direct evidence for training text-enhanced NextItNet entirely from scratch. [ITS-Rec (2025)](https://www.mdpi.com/2079-9292/14/9/1748) combines item IDs with BERT-derived titles, descriptions and reviews; its pretrained encoder and review inputs exceed this task’s constraints. [CLA-Rec (2024)](https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/document/10884256/) uses contrastive alignment to adapt description embeddings to collaborative signals. [CoCoRec (2025)](https://arxiv.org/abs/2503.12183) explicitly addresses the textual–collaborative gap through semantic codes, masked-code modeling and masked-sequence alignment. These provide auxiliary-learning ideas, not evidence that title similarity establishes purchase intent.\n\nA constraint-compatible hypothesis is one jointly trained network: randomly initialized token embeddings, pooled title/description encodings, a learned projection or gate combining text with item IDs, and the existing [NextItNet dilated-convolution residual backbone](https://arxiv.org/abs/1808.05163). Retain next-item prediction as the main objective; test a small auxiliary loss aligning each item’s ID and text representations or predicting target-text features from causal history. This is an adaptation hypothesis, not a demonstrated result from the cited papers. Compare ID-only, text-fusion and fusion-plus-auxiliary variants using fixed macro validation HR@10. Examine errors among textually similar candidates and performance with truncated recent histories to distinguish specific sequential interests from broad topical relevance. Keep one trained checkpoint per category and derive every recommendation score from that network."}
